svg.text: The wrong collection method produces a confident laboratory report about the wrong thing.

g.text: Clean the area, pass the first urine into
the toilet, catch the middle, discard the rest.
The first stream flushes out the organisms
living harmlessly at the urethral opening,
so what you catch came from the bladder.
Clamp briefly, disinfect the sampling port,
withdraw with a sterile syringe, unclamp.
Never take it from the drainage bag: that
urine has been standing for hours and grows
organisms that were never in the patient.
The first urine passed after waking.
It has been concentrating in the bladder
overnight, so scanty things are easier
to find: early pregnancy hormone, acid
fast bacilli, schistosome ova.
Discard the first void and note the time.
Collect everything after it, including the
void at exactly the same time next day.
One forgotten void makes the whole
collection worthless. Start again.

svg.text: DELAY IS ITSELF A FALSE RESULT

g.text: Urine left at room temperature multiplies its own bacteria, so a delayed sample reports an infection that
was not there. Send within an hour, or refrigerate. Write the time of collection on the form, not just the date.
Before collecting anything, ask what question the laboratory is being asked.
Culture, cytology, pregnancy, protein load and drug levels each need a different specimen.
